# pi-coder

Personal setup for coding with pi.

## Vendored SQLite driver

pi-coder uses a script-free vendored `sqlite3@6.0.1` driver with SQLite 3.52.0.
It supports N-API v6 on Linux, macOS, and Windows, including Linux and macOS
ARM64. The loader selects the appropriate platform binary at runtime.

# Delegated agents

The feature is an in-process SDK implementation under `src/tools/agent/`, registered by `src/index.ts`. It lets the parent delegate focused exploration or implementation while preserving pi-coder's permission model, progress UI, and recoverable child sessions. The concise feature contract is in `src/tools/agent/PLAN.md`.

## High-value overview

- Built-ins include read-only `scout` and opt-in `advisor`, command-capable `reviewer`, and the edit-capable permission-gated `worker`; all built-ins load the memory extension. Custom Markdown agents are loaded from `~/.pi/agent/agents` and trusted-project `.pi/agents`; they receive baseline read/search tools and may opt into `memories`, `safe-bash`, or permission-gated `command-runner`. The `memories` capability loads pi-coder's memory extension and adds `~/.pi/agent/memory` as a child read root; definitions can also declare `additionalPaths` read roots and exact `safeBashCommands` patterns.
- The `agent` tool supports `start` (foreground by default, or background with `background=true`), `list`, `status`, `collect`, `continue`, `cancel`, and isolated-result actions. `continue` resumes waiting/interrupted runs or continues collected terminal non-mutating runs. A running foreground `start` or `continue` can be detached to the background with Ctrl+Alt+B; its foreground result returns collection guidance while the child continues. Up to four runs may be active or interrupted; only one mutating worker may run at a time.
- `ask_parent` pauses a child for guidance. Foreground and background children may use restricted `ask_user` when direct user interaction is allowed and the parent is in an interactive TUI; all children may use `ask_parent`, while the advisor remains parent-guidance-only. Full background results remain explicit through `collect`.
- `/agents` browses current/past child sessions, isolated workspaces, and built-in agent model settings. Durable restoration is limited to the exact parent session and active tree branch; interrupted runs never restart or replay automatically.
- Read-only children are cwd-confined plus definition-configured additional read roots; the `memories` capability adds `~/.pi/agent/memory`. Children with Bash access may read exact validated temp files reported in their own truncated Bash result details; `safeBashCommands` extends the curated `safe-bash` set while retaining confinement checks, and `safe-bash` remains heuristic `SAFE_READONLY`, not a security sandbox. Non-isolated command-capable children inherit the parent's Bash permission state; edit-capable workers additionally share same-checkout/outside-cwd file permission behavior. Isolated workspaces keep independent Bash permission state and do not inherit parent-session rules; an explicit remembered Bash rule is also recorded in the parent session for later parent or non-isolated child calls. Changed results remain outside the parent checkout until explicit disposition.
- Agent UI lives in the compositional `src/tui/agents` package. The browser host, session/workspace detail views, workspace browser, and activity widget own generic TUI children rather than extending agent-specific base classes. Shared agent diagnostic formatting belongs in `src/tools/agent/presentation/text.ts`, not the TUI barrel.
- Built-in model overrides are defined in `src/tools/agent/config.ts`, persisted in `~/.pi/agent-config.json` or an existing nearest project `.pi/agent-config.json`, and applied during `AgentLifecycle.discover()` without mutating the shared built-in definitions. Advisor availability is opt-in, persisted alongside those settings, and its runs require an explicit model override.
- Delegated runtime context uses bounded `context.sections` that every agent receives, deduplicated by ID and character-bounded as a block; a definition's optional context policy only narrows (its `sectionIds` and `maxChars`), and an agent without one accepts any ID under the renderer's default budget. Custom/project definitions cannot declare a policy today, so only the advisor narrows. Start (including background starts) returns a non-blocking warning to the parent only for sections actually dropped; automatic parent-summary/recent-context collection remains future work.
- Before release, restore the intended `PI_CODER_AGENT_TRACE=1` opt-in; tracing is currently forced on during development.

# Agent tool reference

This document contains the detailed reference for pi-coder's delegated-agent tool. For the short overview, see [`src/tools/agent/README.md`](src/tools/agent/README.md).

## Actions and lifecycle

| Action     | Behavior                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `start`    | Run an agent in the foreground by default; set `background=true` to start it in the background and return immediately. |
| `list`     | List tracked runs and available workspaces.                                                                            |
| `status`   | Inspect a deliberate snapshot of a run.                                                                                |
| `collect`  | Consume a terminal background result.                                                                                  |
| `continue` | Resume a waiting/interrupted run or continue a collected terminal run.                                                 |
| `cancel`   | Stop a waiting or active run.                                                                                          |
| `inspect`  | Read an isolated result without changing it.                                                                           |
| `apply`    | Apply an isolated result to the parent checkout.                                                                       |
| `retain`   | Keep a result for review while releasing its task lease.                                                               |
| `reset`    | Explicitly reset a workspace for reuse.                                                                                |
| `discard`  | Discard an isolated result or workspace.                                                                               |

There can be up to four active or interrupted runs, and up to three persistent isolated workspaces per repository by default (the limit is configurable in `/agents` Settings). Terminal background results are retained separately until collected or evicted. Continuation lookup is bound to the exact parent session and active parent-tree branch. Continuations retain the same public run ID and physical child identity, so repeated continuations continue the latest checkpoint; isolated workspace results receive new result records while using that same run ID.

### Background behavior

A background `start` returns immediately. Progress appears in the above-editor activity widget and terminal changes are delivered through a coalesced parent mailbox after parent work settles. The mailbox contains only run IDs, statuses, and short previews; use `collect` for the full result. Do not routinely poll with `status` or wait by sleeping.

A running foreground `start` or `continue` can be moved to the background with **Ctrl+Alt+B**. The foreground call returns a short control message immediately; progress and the terminal result are then delivered asynchronously. Retrieve the retained result with `collect` after the terminal notification. This shortcut applies when exactly one detachable foreground operation is active; parallel foreground-call selection is not supported yet.

Foreground and background children may use `ask_user` when direct user interaction is allowed and the parent is running in an interactive TUI. They may use `ask_parent` for parent guidance in any mode. The advisor always uses `ask_parent` because its definition disables direct user interaction. Every agent receives the context sections supplied on `start`; when a narrowing context policy refuses an ID or a repeated ID is dropped, the tool emits a non-blocking warning inside its metadata and continues without that section. Cancellation and shutdown abort active children and close dialogs.

### Interaction and recovery

A waiting child is paused, not completed. An interrupted child was starting or running when shutdown/crash occurred; it is never restarted or replayed automatically. Continuing is an explicit user action and adds an instruction to inspect uncertain state first. Unmatched crash-time tool calls receive synthetic uncertain-outcome errors.

Persisted parent sessions restore waiting/interrupted runs and uncollected terminal outcomes. New, forked, cloned, or ephemeral parent sessions do not inherit them. See [Persistence and recovery](docs/agent-persistence.md).

## Agent roles and definitions

The built-in roles are:

- **`scout`** — read-only reconnaissance.
- **`reviewer`** — read/search plus permission-gated command execution.
- **`worker`** — implementation work with edit/write access; the only edit-capable built-in.
- **`advisor`** — read-only senior advice, disabled until assigned a model in `/agents`.

Custom definitions live in `~/.pi/agent/agents/*.md` or trusted project `.pi/agents/*.md` files. They always receive baseline read/search access. Optional capabilities are `memories`, `scratchpad`, `todolist`, `safe-bash`, and `command-runner`; `edit` is reserved for the built-in worker. Trusted project definitions override user definitions. Built-in names are reserved.

Two capabilities imply others, because they are strengths of one axis rather than independent grants: `command-runner` implies `safe-bash`, and `todolist` implies `scratchpad`. Implications are applied where a definition is read, so the parent-facing catalog and the persisted definition fingerprint both describe the same effective grant.

A definition may select a model and narrow the bounded context sections it accepts. An agent without a policy receives every section it is given under the renderer's default budget, so only a listed policy can refuse IDs. Dynamic parent/repository/workspace context belongs in the initial task message, not the system prompt, so the child transcript retains it exactly.

## Capabilities, grants, and gates

What a definition declares and what a child can actually do are separated into five layers, each with one job. Keeping them apart is what lets a capability be read in one file instead of inferred from six scattered conditions.

| Layer       | Location               | Owns                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Declaration | `definitions/types.ts` | capability names, baseline grants, implications, the authority ladder, and the fingerprint over the _declared_ set |
| Grant       | `child/grant.ts`       | the single resolution from a definition plus run mode plus parent UI to one `ChildGrant`                           |
| Units       | `child/capabilities/`  | per capability: the session tools it adds, the read roots it publishes, and the extension it registers             |

# Compaction

pi owns compaction; pi-coder replaces it with one `session_before_compact` handler in
`src/modules/compaction/index.ts` (`registerCompactionExtension`), installed for the parent from
`src/index.ts` and for every child as the `pi-coder-compaction` entry in
`src/tools/agent/child/index.ts:childExtensionEntries`. Read pi's `docs/compaction.md` and
`dist/core/compaction/compaction.js` before changing this; every invariant below came from reading core, not
from guessing. Returning `undefined` hands the compaction back to core.

## Why

Core serializes the summarized span (`serializeConversation`): `[Assistant thinking]:` **untruncated**, tool
results at a non-exported fixed 2000 chars, no overall budget — then sends it with `cacheRetention: "none"`
and a fresh `sessionId`, so all of that bulk is billed as fresh input. Thinking is normally the largest block
in a session, and pi keeps thinking in the live context anyway (`hideThinkingBlock` is display-only).

## Pipeline

1. **segment (stage 1, native)** — `span-session.ts` copies pi's resolved context entries
   (`ctx.sessionManager.buildContextEntries()`) truncated at `preparation.firstKeptEntryId` into
   `SessionManager.inMemory(cwd)`, and `convertToLlm(spanManager.buildSessionContext().messages)` yields the
   discarded span as **real message objects** — previous checkpoint included, retained tail excluded. Built
   with the parent's `ctx.getSystemPrompt()` and its active tools in `agent.state.tools` order, so the request
   is a strict shorter prefix of what the provider already cached. Tools stay in the request - removing them
   would move the prefix - and the prohibition is the instruction text, because `tool_choice` is not sent (see
   **`tool_choice` is not sent** below). Stage 1 also forwards the session's thinking level as `reasoningEffort`
   so the thinking parameters match pi's turn requests (**stage 1 forwards the thinking level** below); stage 2
   deliberately does not. A `toolCall` block in the response rejects the stage; a call the server
   leaves unparsed arrives as text and is **not** detected. Stage 1 and stage 2 get the **same** output cap (see
   "The budgets behind the fit test" - a cap that binds discards a checkpoint whole) and stage 1 is told it is an
   intermediate, because a generous intermediate becomes a rival draft: measured before any cap existed, stage 1
   wrote 3,207 tokens and the reduce then produced something *longer* than the material it was handed. That risk is
   carried by the instruction and the report's ratio, not by a smaller cap.
2. **reduce (stage 2, serialized)** — one bounded text-only call over `serializeConversationMinimal(span)` +
   stage 1's `<segment-checkpoint>`, plus `<previous-summary>` **only when stage 1 did not run** (stage 1's
   instruction already carries it forward, so feeding both invites a union of duplicates). Transcript-first on
   disagreement, checkpoint fills what compression removed, and the output must be no longer than the
   checkpoint it was given — merge and drop, never concatenate.
3. **core default** — `undefined`.

The fit gate is `nativeRequestFits`, and `fitRequirementTokens` decides what it measures against the window, best
evidence first: the **exact-cut** count (the provider's own `input + cacheRead + cacheWrite` for the reply sitting
*at* the cut point, whose request body was exactly this span — see **Requests are sized from the session's own
counts**), then the **span-anchored** count (a provider's `usage.totalTokens` for a reply inside the span, plus
chars/4 only for what followed it and for the appended instruction), then **`ctx.getContextUsage().tokens`**, then
the whole-body chars/4 guess. Every count tier is filtered by `countBoundary`: a number that predates the newest
`compaction`, `model_change`, or `thinking_level_change` row describes a body that no longer exists and is
rejected, counted in `staleAnchors`. The last tier is *not* the provider's count of the request — it counts the
retained tail stage 1 drops, and it is `null` right after a compaction, which is when compaction usually runs. A
hot estimate alone used to skip stage 1 on ~200k windows; the counts are what removed that and the tail's
inflation.

## Continue at a glance

`continue` resumes a waiting or interrupted child, or continues a collected terminal child run in the existing child conversation. Waiting and interrupted runs use their existing live or restored handle; collected runs reopen the persisted child session and exact transcript leaf. For an isolated collected run, it keeps the same workspace; for a non-mutating run such as `reviewer`, it reuses the original execution cwd without a workspace. Resolution is restricted to the exact parent session and active parent-tree branch. It uses the persisted definition snapshot (including capabilities and role prompt), preserves the recorded model, and sends the supplied guidance as the next prompt. A current definition fingerprint mismatch is informational; snapshots without the definition contract fail clearly. It keeps the same public run ID; continue using that ID for later actions.

Before continuing a collected isolated run, the worktree `HEAD` must descend from the recorded workspace base. Divergent history is rejected without starting the child or changing the existing result. The existing workspace lease remains held throughout continuation and finalization; failures preserve it for explicit recovery.

## pi-coder — overview

**What it is:** a single, personal pi extension (`package.json` → `pi.extensions: ["./src/index.ts"]`) that layers coding-oriented memory, a bash sandbox, delegated-agent orchestration, and a richer TUI on top of `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`. **Entry point:** `src/index.ts` — a flat list of `register*` calls. Everything is installed from there; anything not reachable from it doesn't exist.

### The four big pillars (by size)

| Area | Path | LOC | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Delegated agents** | `src/tools/agent/` | 20,105 (96 files) | In-process `agent` tool. Built-ins: `scout` (read-only), `reviewer` (command-gated), `worker` (only edit-capable), `advisor` (opt-in). Custom Markdown agents from `~/.pi/agent/agents` + project `.pi/agents`. Actions `start/list/status/collect/continue/cancel/inspect/apply/retain/reset/discard`, foreground + background, mailbox delivery, persistent Git-worktree isolation with leases, durable session restore, `/agents` browser UI. |
| **Bash sandbox** | `src/modules/sandbox/` | 7,898 (28 files) | A hand-written bash AST parser (`bash.ts`) + cwd-confinement heuristics (`heuristics/`) that decide which commands are `SAFE_READONLY` and which need a prompt, plus a `bwrap` bubblewrap jail (`bubblewrap.ts`), a curated command registry (`commands/`), permission state, session-scoped rule suggestions, and a decision log mined for new heuristics. |
| **Compaction** | `src/modules/compaction/` | 6,817 (18 files) | Replaces pi's own summarization for the parent *and* every child via one `session_before_compact` handler. Two-stage: a native span read (shorter-prefix-of-cached-request, to preserve prefix cache) then a bounded serialized reduce. Includes a fit gate sized from the provider's own usage counts, a hash-chain ledger, and an extensive trace system. |
| **TUI** | `src/tui/` | 6,139 (27 files) | Shared primitives — `list-view.ts` (ListViewComponent base for pager/select/multi-select) and `inline-editor.ts` (the cursor/paste/navigation engine behind ask-user and select-with-message) — plus `agents/` compositional browser and `status/` widgets (agent activity, todolist). Architectural rule: extend these, don't duplicate them. |

### Smaller modules & tools

- `src/modules/memory/` (405) — indexed frontmatter memories at `.pi/agent/memory/` + `~/.pi/agent/memory/`, injected into the system prompt.
- `src/modules/todolist/` (856) — private per-runtime `TODO.md` with YAML frontmatter, a bash guard, and progress events.
- `src/modules/scratchpad/` (165) — session-scoped private temp directory, an agent capability, multi-root confined.
- `src/tools/{bash,read,write,file-permissions}` — hooks wrapping pi's own tools so file and command access share one guarding path.

- **Capability split is sacred:** scout read-only → reviewer/worker command-capable → only worker edits. Kept as five separate layers (declaration → grant → units → gates → prompt) so a capability is readable in one file.
- **Style:** ES2023+ array methods over hand-rolled loops, guard clauses over nesting, mandatory braces, one-responsibility functions.

## Component catalog

Five layers: **registered surface → feature modules → tools → shared TUI → common infra**. Everything hangs off `src/index.ts`.

---

### 1. Registered surface (what the extension installs into pi)

| Kind | Name | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Tool | `agent` | `src/tools/agent/presentation/tool.ts:144` |
| Tool | `ask_user` | `src/tools/ask_user/index.ts:7` |
| Tool (child-side) | `ask_user`, `ask_parent` | `src/tools/agent/child/gates/interaction.ts:100,171` |
| Command | `/agents` | `src/tools/agent/browser.ts:465` |
| Command | `/agent-trace` | `src/tools/agent/observability/trace.ts:203` |
| Command | `/bash-sandbox-config` | `src/commands/config.ts:251` |
| Shortcut | `ctrl+alt+b` (detach foreground child to background) | `src/tools/agent/index.ts:35` |
| Hooks | `tool_call`/`tool_result` on `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`; `session_before_compact`; `before_provider_request`; `session_start`/`_shutdown`/`_tree`; `before_agent_start`; `message_start`/`_update` | the `register*` calls in `src/index.ts` |

---

### 2. Feature modules — `src/modules/`

**`sandbox/` (7,898 lines, 28 files)** — the bash + path permission engine. Components:

- `bash.ts` (1,211) — hand-written **bash AST parser**: `parseBashAst` → `BashAst` / `BashStatement` / `BashCommand` nodes with word kinds, expansion flags (`tilde|glob|brace|variable`), heredocs, substitutions, redirections. The substrate everything else reasons over.
- `commands/` (12 files) — a **declarative command registry**: `KNOWN_COMMANDS` merged from readers, text, vcs, directories, archives, checksums, comparison, sed, mutators, system. Each `CommandSpec` declares safe flags, `FlagSpec` value counts, path slots, and `unsafe` markers. `VALUE`/`PATH_VALUE`/`OUTPUT_PATH_VALUE`/`UNSAFE` are the shared vocabulary.
- `heuristics/` — **cwd-confinement judgement** (not a security sandbox, heuristic `SAFE_READONLY`):
  - `command-access.ts` (1,058) — per-command operand inspection, custom safe-bash matching, expansion refusals.
  - `evaluator.ts` (786) — `isCommandConfined` / `isConfined`, chain-operator handling.
  - `path-policy.ts` (548) — `resolvePath`, `isSensitivePath`, `isRealPathConfined`, `hasSymlinkComponent`, `isHardLinkedFileOperand`, `canonicalizePath`, `buildConfinementOptions`.
  - `glob-expansion.ts` — `expandGlobPattern` answering only "which operands can the shell pass?" (`*`/`?` only; bracket expressions deliberately refused).
  - `index.ts` — the public `get*Assessment` / `get*Permission` façade; `types.ts` holds `UnsafeReason` + assessment constructors.
- `permissions.ts` (752) — **user-configured rules**, four-valued lattice `deny | ask | allow | allow:sandbox` with `moreRestrictive()` and pattern matchers that understand subshells and incomplete substitutions. `resolve.ts` produces the per-segment `ResolvePermissionDetails` (which commands went uncovered) used by the dialog.
- `bubblewrap.ts` (206+) — emits the `bwrap` command line that actually jails an allowed command.
- `command-wrappers.ts` — strips `timeout`/`nice`-style wrapper prefixes before assessment.
- `permission-state.ts` — per-session state: granted rules, remembered approvals, isolation from parent state for worktree children.
- `suggestions.ts` — `suggestRule(tokens)` generating the session-scoped "allow this next time" rules offered in the prompt.
- `decision-log.ts` — appends every prompt/outcome to a JSONL log mined for new heuristics (`scripts/permission-report.ts`, `docs/bash-decision-log.md`).

**`compaction/` (6,817, 18 files)** — replaces pi's summarizer for parent *and* every child. Pipeline components:

- `index.ts` (1,268) — the `session_before_compact` handler and `before_provider_request` observer; owns stage sequencing, budgets (`summarizationBudgetTokens`), and the `undefined` hand-back to core.
- `span-session.ts` — builds an in-memory `SessionManager` over the discarded span so stage 1 gets **real message objects** that are a strict shorter prefix of the cached request.
- `native-request.ts` (550) — the fit machinery: `buildNativeContext`, `countSpanTokens`, `countBoundary`/`contextIsStale` (rejecting provider counts that predate a `compaction`/`model_change`/`thinking_level_change`), `fitRequirementTokens`, `nativeRequestFits`.
- `ledger.ts` (541) — measured body accounting across folds: `measureEntries`, `headAt`, `foldNet(s)`, `bodyTokens`, `estimatedShare`, `correctAcrossFolds`.
- `usage.ts` / `text.ts` / `cut.ts` — char-4 estimation, `estimateWireMessages`, `chooseSpanCut` + `measureSpanAt`.
- `serialize.ts` (328+) — `serializeConversationMinimal`, the bounded transcript-first text handed to stage 2.
- `sections.ts` / `prompt.ts` — `analyzeSpan` → supplementary sections and file lists; the stage-1 checkpoint and stage-2 reduce instructions.
- `summarize.ts` / `failure.ts` — the two calls plus `classifySummarizationFailure` / `summarizationFailureAction` (terminal vs. fall-back causes).
- `chain.ts` (758) + `chain-store.ts` + `prefix-diff.ts` — `RequestChain` hash-chain of request shapes, `fingerprintPayload`, divergence reporting against the provider cache.
- `trace.ts` / `config.ts` / `types.ts` — JSONL trace recorder, config loading, `summarizedSpan`.

**`memory/` (405)** — `scanMemories` + `parseFrontmatter` + `formatMemoryList`; injects the indexed memory list on `session_start` / `before_agent_start`, refreshes on compact and message updates.

**`todolist/` (856)** — `parseTodoList` (YAML frontmatter + freeform body), `persistence.ts` snapshots appended to the session, `progress.ts` summarization, `events.ts` bus emission, `bash-guard.ts` (protects `TODO.md` from `rm`/truncation), status widget feed.

**`scratchpad/` (165)** — session-scoped temp dir: creation, `getScratchpadPath`, shutdown marker, prompt paragraph. Doubles as an agent capability and a confinement root.

---

### 3. Tools — `src/tools/`

- **`agent/` (20,105, 96 files)** — split into seven packages:
  - `definitions/` — `discovery.ts` holds the four built-ins (scout/reviewer/worker/advisor) and loads user `~/.pi/agent/agents/*.md` + project `.pi/agents/*.md` (project wins, built-in names reserved); `types.ts` owns `AGENT_CAPABILITIES` (read, search, memories, scratchpad, todolist, safe-bash, command-runner, edit), `BASELINE_AGENT_CAPABILITIES`, the **authority ladder** `read → inspect → command → mutate`, implications, and the declared-set fingerprint; `validate.ts` + `prompt.ts` for frontmatter and role prompts; `renderer.ts` in `prompts/` for bounded `context.sections`.
  - `child/` — the child runtime. `grant.ts` is the *single* resolution of definition + run mode + parent UI into one `ChildGrant`; `capabilities/` has one unit per capability (tools it adds, read roots it publishes, extension it registers); `gates/` installs **five hooks in a test-pinned order** — `bash-output` (ledger of live temp paths) → `file-access` (records end-user approvals before others read them) → `interaction` (registers child tools) → `commands` (claims `edit`/`write`/`bash` at rung `command`+, serializing them) → `confinement` (last, so approvals already applied). Plus `transcript.ts` (bootstrap/open/`selectChildSessionLeaf`/`repairInterruptedToolCalls`), `model-runtime.ts` (child model + API key resolution), `progress.ts` (usage aggregation, tracker snapshots, mutation report), `safe-bash.ts` + `safe-bash-rules.ts`, `roots.ts`, `prompt/` (paragraph builders for paths, interaction, reporting, profiles).
  - `runs/` — orchestration. `manager.ts` (2,158) is the state machine behind all actions; `registry.ts` (run identity), `run-state.ts` (statuses + guidance constants), `restore.ts` (durable recovery), `projection.ts` (run → details/outcome/summary), `checkpoint-store.ts`, `continuation-lease.ts` (pid-liveness leases, `CONTINUATION_LEASE_MS`), `usage.ts`, `child-setup.ts`, and `persistence/` (`load`, `state-writer`, `stored-record` validation + working-state overlay, `journal-heads`, `lease-ledger`, `session-paths`, `catalog-projection`).
  - `workspaces/` — isolated git worktrees: `store.ts` (claim/lease/recycle, `MAX_AGENT_WORKSPACES`), `lifecycle.ts` (lease recovery), `setup.ts` (optional setup run + prompts), `results.ts` (988 — `apply`/`retain`/`discard`/`reset`), `checkpoints.ts`, `finalization.ts`, `parent-actions.ts` + `actions.ts` + `tui-actions.ts`, `git.ts`.
  - `storage/` — sqlite persistence: `metadata.ts` (migrations, workspaces root), `run-catalog.ts`, `run-snapshots.ts`, `run-state.ts`, `run-working-state.ts`, `run-markers.ts`.
  - `presentation/` — `tool.ts` (schema), `outcomes.ts`, `status.ts`, `mailbox.ts` (coalesced parent notifications), `sessions.ts`, `transcript.ts`, `todo-transcript.ts`, `text.ts` (shared diagnostics), `formatting.ts`, `browser-models.ts`.
  - `observability/` — `events.ts` (`pi-coder:agent-event` bus adapter) and `trace.ts` (`AgentTraceStore`, `/agent-trace`).
  - Top level: `lifecycle.ts` (`AgentLifecycle` composition), `browser.ts` (`/agents`), `action-dispatch.ts` (`executeAgentAction`), `config.ts` (model overrides, advisor enablement, workspace cap, `~/.pi/agent-config.json` or nearest `.pi/agent-config.json`), `contracts/` (context, events, mutations, runs, trace, workspaces).
- **`bash/` (448)** — the `tool_call` hook that turns the sandbox into behavior: parse → heuristic + rules → sandboxed exec or the permission dialog (`selectWithMessage`), session rule memory, decision logging, `tool_result` truncation.
- **`file-permissions.ts` (shared by `read/` and `write/`)** — one guard parameterized per tool: read roots (cwd, memory dir, scratchpad, `additionalPaths`), write confinement, approval prompts, audit entries.
- **`ask_user/` (127)** — thin tool wrapper over the TUI component.

---

### 4. Shared TUI — `src/tui/` (6,139, 27 files)

- `list-view.ts` (512) — **`ListViewComponent` base** every list dialog extends (state, `calculateScrollOffset`, prefix rendering); the architectural rule is to extend this, not copy it.
- `inline-editor.ts` (935) — **the text-editing engine**: cursor, visual-line, atomic paste, `LARGE_PASTE_THRESHOLD`; backs ask-user and select-with-message. Invariants documented in the `edit-cursor-navigation` memory.
- Dialogs composed from those two: `pager.ts`, `select.ts`, `multi-select.ts`, `select-with-message.ts` (561 — the permission dialog), `ask-user.ts` (424), `confirmation.ts`, `numeric-input.ts`.
- `dialog-queue.ts` — serializes concurrent dialogs (`withDialogQueue`, `isDialogActive`, `TUI_DIALOG_EVENT`); `overlay-stack.ts` — binds a component as a pi overlay (`withOverlayStack`); `spinner.ts`; `border-box.ts` (border character sets); `markdown-theme.ts`.
- `agents/` — the `/agents` browser package: `browser.ts` (941 — `AgentSessionBrowserComponent`), `session-detail.ts`, `workspace.ts` (detail + browser), `refresh.ts` (`RefreshCoordinator`), `formatting.ts`, `types.ts`. Composes the generic primitives rather than subclassing agent-specific bases.
- `status/` — `widget.ts` (`PiCoderStatusWidget` host), `agent-activity-widget.ts` (live background-child activity above the editor), `todolist-widget.ts`, plus the two formatters.

---

### 5. Common infra — `src/common/` (1,656)

`sqlite.ts` (`SqliteDatabase` + `migrateSqliteDatabase`, over the vendored script-free `sqlite3@6.0.1` in `vendor/sqlite3/`) · `record-log.ts` (generation-discovering JSONL append log — shared by decision log and compaction traces) · `config.ts` (sandbox + model config) · `constants.ts`, `paths.ts`, `slug.ts`, `frontmatter.ts`, `text.ts` (indent/truncate/wrap), `home-directory.ts` (`resolveHomeDirectory`, so certified and shell-opened paths agree), `abort.ts`, `async.ts`, `audit.ts`, `trace.ts` (`isAgentTraceEnabled`).

Supporting: `src/commands/config.ts` (the sandbox config editor), `prompts/init.md`, `skills/memory-prune/`, `scripts/{permission-report,compaction-report}.ts` + two Python reporters.

# src/tui component architecture

Shared composable TUI building blocks, extracted to deduplicate dialog and activity-widget behavior:

- **`list-view.ts`** — `ListViewComponent<T, R, S>` base class: frame scaffolding (DynamicBorder/title/header/footer/help), configurable `borderColor`, border glyphs, optional header spacing, fixed-height/compact-footer framing, visual-line wrapping, item render cache, cursor-follow scrolling, scroll indicator, ↑/↓/j/k nav, `onKey` hook. Subclass extension points: `getItemPrefix()`, `handleAction()`, `onExternalDone()`, `renderStatus()`, plus compositional `itemPrefix`, `onCacheBuilt`, title, and help updates. Subclasses: `pager.ts`, `select.ts`, and `multi-select.ts`; `SelectComponent` supports opt-in printable-input filtering with a header search indicator via `enableSearch`. The agent browser is now a composed host in `agents/browser.ts`. The unified browser defaults its Agents view to the current parent session, with an `h` toggle for cwd-wide historical sessions, plus Workspaces and Settings views; it opens pager-based read-only session or workspace metadata views.
- **`dialog-queue.ts`** — shared abort-aware FIFO for modal `ctx.ui.custom()` dialogs. `askUser()` and `selectWithMessage()` both use it; future permission dialogs must use one of these queued entrypoints rather than calling `ctx.ui.custom()` directly. Queued cancellation returns promptly without allowing later dialogs to overtake the active one.
- **`confirmation.ts`** — reusable `ConfirmationComponent` and `confirm()` helper for centered, focus-safe yes/no overlays. The helper participates in `withOverlayStack`, so it can be opened from an existing overlay; the delegated-agent browser uses it for agent cancellation and workspace disposition actions.
- **`inline-editor.ts`** — `InlineEditor`: theme-free inline edit engine (segment buffer with atomic paste placeholders, bracketed paste, pi-tui-matching word movement/deletion, display↔content mapping, windowed `renderLines()` returning plain strings). Composed by `ask-user.ts`, `select-with-message.ts`, and `numeric-input.ts`; callers supply styling via pre-styled prefixes/placeholders and set `editor.focused`.
- **`numeric-input.ts`** — `NumericInputComponent<T extends number>`: reusable modal inline numeric editor with caller-provided parsing/validation, built on `InlineEditor` and `BorderBox`; its `numericInput()` helper opens the component through `withOverlayStack`. Use it for settings that need arbitrary numeric values instead of fixed choice lists.
- **`spinner.ts`** — `Spinner`: small reusable animated frame component with configurable frames/interval, `setActive()`, and `dispose()`. It requests TUI renders while active, pauses on the shared `pi-coder:tui-dialog` EventBus event, and is used by the delegated-agent activity widget.
- **`agents/`** — Agent-specific browser TUI package. Its browser, session/workspace details, and workspace browser implement `Component` and compose the generic list/pager/select components. Agent browser imports should use this package directly. Session-transcript projections, including TODO transcript formatting, belong under `src/tools/agent/presentation/` rather than the status-widget package.
- **`status/`** — Shared parent status package. Its composite widget, agent activity/TODO renderers, and status-widget formatters combine agent activity and TODO sections under one above-editor registration; domain modules publish typed `pi.events` snapshots on `pi-coder:status-agent` and `pi-coder:status-todo`, while the status package alone owns widget registration and event listeners.
- `ListViewComponent` fits fixed-height frames by reserving space for scroll indicators/wrapped footers and placing a flexible spacer before help text, so compact agent detail/workspace views anchor help at the bottom; it restores the configured viewport size when dimensions change. It caches rendered and wrapped item lines across scroll-only renders; `invalidate()` marks that cache dirty for content changes, while custom key handlers use the non-cache-invalidating path for offset-only navigation.
- `AgentSessionDetailComponent` clamps its pager scroll offset after transcript content changes, which is required when switching from a long detailed transcript to a shorter collapsed one. When an open live run transitions to a historical row without preloaded transcript text, the browser must trigger the lazy transcript loader again before the detail can retain the final transcript/TODO projection. When a lazy transcript resolves, update the open detail before invalidating cached browser state, then call the host `onInvalidate` callback so the TUI redraws without waiting for another keypress.
- Agent transcript formatting collects ordered conversation entries separately from one optional TODO entry. The renderer inserts that TODO immediately after the initial user context (or at the start when no user entry exists), then applies detailed or collapsed tool-call rendering. The session detail overlay receives structured transcript parts, renders prose through Markdown, and emits tool-call parts as plain lines. Detailed edit/write calls default to concise changed-line counts; the formatter retains an opt-in constant for full diff lines if that presentation is desired later. Presentation tests cover ordering and browser snapshots cover the resulting TUI.

Tests: `test/` (vitest). `test/inline-editor.test.ts` unit-tests the editor engine; `test/helpers.ts` provides the headless harness for component rendering tests (`mockTheme` identity theme, `KEY` raw key map, `press`/`type`/`paste`, `interact()` which renders after every keypress like the real TUI loop — needed because InlineEditor up/down reads render-computed visual-line state, and `renderText()` which strips CURSOR_MARKER and renders inverse-video cursor chars as `[X]`). TUI rendering tests use file snapshots. Agent UI imports use the composed `src/tui/agents` package; add focused package tests when extending its controller/lifecycle behavior. When changing edit behavior, change InlineEditor once — both dialogs inherit it.

description: Layout invariants that prevent permission-dialog flickering when content exceeds terminal height.
category: architecture
---

# Permission dialog layout

`src/tui/select-with-message.ts` keeps the title short and puts long command text in a capped, scrollable content area. The content area renders numbered, manually wrapped lines; selection items and help text remain below it and visible. PageUp/PageDown update the content scroll offset.

Wrapping uses `wrapTextWithAnsi` for command content and `wrapPreservingSpaces` through `InlineEditor` for in-progress feedback, so trailing spaces remain visible while typing. The edit area is capped at three visual lines and uses a cursor-safe window; the cursor is never placed on a truncated first/last line.

`InlineEditor` is shared by `select-with-message.ts` and `ask-user.ts`. Keep layout and editing fixes in the shared editor where possible, and preserve the render-after-input behavior used by `test/helpers.ts` because vertical cursor movement depends on render-computed visual-line state.
---
name: edit-cursor-navigation
description: Cursor, paste, and visual-line navigation invariants for the shared InlineEditor.
category: architecture
---

# InlineEditor navigation

`src/tui/inline-editor.ts` owns a flat content cursor (`cursorPos`) over segment content. Segments are typed text or atomic large-paste placeholders. The public buffer is exposed as `text`; callers use `handlePasteInput()`, `handleKey()`, and `renderLines()`.

## Atomic paste behavior

Cursor movement skips over paste segments. Backspace/delete at a paste boundary removes the entire segment. Word movement and deletion use `Intl.Segmenter` refined with ASCII punctuation boundaries, then clamp boundaries so they never land inside a paste segment. Range deletion removes any overlapping paste marker and merges adjacent text segments.

## Display mapping and wrapping

`renderLines()` builds a display buffer with paste placeholders and maintains content-to-display and display-to-content mappings. It wraps hard lines with `wrapPreservingSpaces`, records `EditVisLine` ranges, maps the cursor to an absolute visual-line index, and returns a window of rendered strings with optional ellipsis indicators. The caller supplies prefixes, placeholders, and styling.

Up/down uses the absolute visual-line state computed during the last render and remembers the desired column. Because adjacent visual lines share a boundary, boundary mapping must use exclusive ends and special-case the final end-of-buffer position. Up on the first visual line goes to buffer start; down on the last goes to buffer end.

The edit width reserves one cell for the cursor. The maximum visible edit-line count must be at least three so the cursor remains on a non-truncated middle line. Bracketed paste data may arrive in chunks; inactive pastes are consumed and discarded.

`InlineEditor` is composed by both `src/tui/ask-user.ts` and `src/tui/select-with-message.ts`; change the engine once rather than duplicating editing behavior. Tests live in `test/inline-editor.test.ts` and component snapshots use `test/helpers.ts`.

## `src/tui/` — 26 files, 6,139 lines, three tiers

```
primitives (7)  →  dialogs (7)  →  domain packages (agents/, status/)
```

The architectural rule from `AGENTS.md` and the `tui-components` memory: **extend these, never duplicate them.** When an editing or layout fix is needed, it goes into `InlineEditor` or `ListViewComponent` once and both dialogs inherit it.

---

### Tier 0 — primitives (no theme assumptions, reusable frame plumbing)

**`border-box.ts` (145)** — `BorderBox` component + `BorderCharacters` interface and five glyph sets: `ROUNDED_BORDER`, `LIGHT_BORDER`, `HEAVY_BORDER`, `DOUBLE_BORDER`, `MIXED_BORDER`, aggregated in `BORDER_STYLES`. Every framed dialog/overlay draws through it; `truncateToWidth` keeps titles from overflowing.

**`list-view.ts` (512)** — `ListViewComponent<T, R, S extends ListViewState<T>>`, **the base class all list dialogs share**. It owns the parts that used to be copy-pasted: frame scaffolding (DynamicBorder + title + header/footer slots), configurable `borderColor` and glyphs, optional header spacing, fixed-height / compact-footer framing, visual-line wrapping, a **per-item render cache** (`invalidate()` marks dirty on content change; offset-only navigation takes the non-invalidating path), cursor-follow scrolling for multi-line items, the scroll indicator, `↑/↓/j/k`, and the `onKey` interception hook. Subclass extension points only: `getItemPrefix()`, `handleAction()`, `onExternalDone()`, `renderStatus()`, plus compositional `itemPrefix` / `onCacheBuilt` / title+help updates. Fits fixed-height frames by reserving room for indicators and wrapped footers and placing a flexible spacer before help text, restoring viewport size on dimension change.

**`inline-editor.ts` (935)** — `InlineEditor`, **the theme-free single-field text engine**. Owns a segment buffer (typed text + atomic large-paste placeholders above `LARGE_PASTE_THRESHOLD = 150`), bracketed paste (including chunked pastes, and discarding inactive ones), pi-tui-matching char/word/visual-line movement and word deletion (`Intl.Segmenter` refined with ASCII punctuation stops, clamped so boundaries never land inside a paste segment), display↔content mapping, and windowed `renderLines()` that returns **plain strings** — callers supply prefixes, placeholders, and styling, and set `editor.focused`. Deliberately knows nothing about `Theme`/`Container`/`Text` so it composes into any layout. Hard-won invariants (see the `edit-cursor-navigation` memory): cursor skips whole paste segments; backspace at a boundary deletes the entire segment; up/down uses render-computed visual-line state so a render must happen first; edit width reserves one cell for the cursor; max visible edit lines ≥ 3 so the cursor never sits on a truncated line.

**`dialog-queue.ts` (111)** — abort-aware **FIFO for modal `ctx.ui.custom()` dialogs**, keyed per `EventBus`: `withDialogQueue(signal, fn)`, `isDialogActive(events)`, `hasQueuedDialog(events)`, emitting `pi-coder:tui-dialog` (`TUI_DIALOG_EVENT`). Cancelled entries return promptly without letting later dialogs overtake the active one. Rule: permission dialogs must enter through a queued entrypoint (`askUser`/`selectWithMessage`), never `ctx.ui.custom()` directly.

**`overlay-stack.ts` (158)** — `withOverlayStack` + `OverlayStackBinding` + internal `OverlayStackManager`: makes nested overlays possible by installing a TUI input listener that remembers focus before pi's catch-all and re-focuses the top overlay *before* the key is dispatched. This is what lets `confirm()` / `numericInput()` open from inside the already-open `/agents` browser.

**`spinner.ts` (91)** — `Spinner` with `DEFAULT_SPINNER_FRAMES`, `setActive()`, `dispose()`; requests renders while active and **pauses on the dialog event** so its animation doesn't fight a modal for the screen.

**`markdown-theme.ts` (23)** — `markdownTheme(theme)`, mapping pi's `Theme` onto pi-tui's `MarkdownTheme`; the only consumer is the `agent` tool's own result rendering (`src/tools/agent/presentation/tool.ts`).

---

### Tier 1 — dialogs (each = a component class + an async `fn()` helper)

| File | Component / helper | What it is | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pager.ts` (134) | `PagerComponent` / `pager()` | Read-only scrollable list — `PagerState.cursor = null`, scroll driven externally; `PagerItem`, custom `renderItem`, header/footer. | `/agent-trace` (`observability/trace.ts`), the sandbox config command (`commands/config.ts`) |
| `select.ts` (201) | `SelectComponent` / `select()` | Single-choice list with `→ ` prefix, `initialCursor`, `maxVisible`, `onKey`; `enableSearch` adds printable-input filtering plus a header search indicator and swaps the help line. | agent browser (`agents/browser.ts`) |
| `multi-select.ts` (198) | `MultiSelectComponent` / `multiSelect()` | Checkboxes — `→ [x] ` prefix, `MultiSelectState` extends base state with `selected: Set<number>`, `initialSelected`, toggle-all. | available to dialogs (currently no non-test consumer) |
| `select-with-message.ts` (561) | `SelectWithMessageComponent` / `selectWithMessage()` | **The permission dialog.** Short title + a capped, scrollable numbered content area (PageUp/PageDown) with items and help always visible below — the layout that fixed the flicker (`tui-flickering-fix` memory). `title` and `borderTone` may be **functions re-evaluated every render** (live mode indicator, accent border while in edit mode); items carry per-item `placeholder`; result is `{ value, message, displayText }`. Hides the working spinner while open. | the three permission sites: `src/tools/bash/index.ts`, `src/tools/file-permissions.ts` (read/write/edit), `src/tools/agent/child/command-permissions.ts`, plus `workspaces/setup.ts` |
| `ask-user.ts` (424) | `AskUserComponent` / `askUser()` | The `ask_user` tool's UI: option list with descriptions, a trailing custom-answer entry (`customOptionLabel`), an inline `InlineEditor` message field, returning `{ answer, isCustom, optionIndex }`; degrades to `undefined` when `!ctx.hasUI` or aborted. | `src/tools/ask_user/index.ts` and the child `ask_user`/`ask_parent` tools (`child/gates/interaction.ts`) |
| `confirmation.ts` (121) | `ConfirmationComponent` / `confirm()` | Centered, focus-safe yes/no overlay that participates in `withOverlayStack`, so it can open on top of another overlay. | `src/tools/agent/browser.ts` (run cancellation, workspace disposition) |
| `numeric-input.ts` (176) | `NumericInputComponent<T extends number>` / `numericInput()`, `parsePositiveInteger()` | Modal inline numeric editor over `InlineEditor` + `BorderBox`, with **caller-provided parsing/validation** (`{value} \| {error}`), opened through the overlay stack. For settings that need arbitrary numbers rather than a fixed choice list. | `src/tools/agent/browser.ts` (setting an agent's model/limit) |

---

### Tier 2 — `agents/` and `status/` (domain packages that *compose* Tier 0/1)

**`agents/` (1,585 lines) — the `/agents` browser.** Registered by `src/tools/agent/browser.ts:465`.

- `browser.ts` (941) — `AgentSessionBrowserComponent` + `showAgentWorkspaceBrowser`. Notably it extends `ListViewComponent` with its own `BrowserState` carrying a **`tab: "agents" | "workspaces" | "settings"`** and a **`scope: "session" | "historical"`** (the `h` toggle; default is the current parent session), union-typing items across sessions/workspace rows/`AgentSetting`, with `isWorkspace`/`isSetting` guards. Opens read-only pager-style details, subscribes to `AGENT_EVENT_CHANNEL` to refresh live rows, lazily loads transcripts, and calls out to `confirm()` / `numericInput()` / `SelectComponent` as child overlays.
- `session-detail.ts` (220) — `AgentSessionDetailComponent`: transcript viewer that **clamps its scroll offset after content changes** (required when a long detailed transcript switches to a collapsed one) and renders prose through Markdown while tool calls stay plain lines; edit/write calls default to changed-line counts.
- `workspace.ts` (377) — `AgentWorkspaceDetailComponent`, `AgentWorkspaceBrowserComponent`, `showAgentWorkspaceBrowser`, and the `AgentWorkspaceAction` union.
- `formatting.ts` (217) — pure view-model → label builders: `asSessionListItems`, `asWorkspaceListItems`, `asSettingsListItems`, `agentWorkspaceItemText`, `workspaceDetailText`/`…HelpText`, `oneLine`, `compactNumber`, `dateText`, `usageText`, `returnedText`, plus the `EMPTY_AGENTS` / `EMPTY_WORKSPACES` sentinels.
- `refresh.ts` (48) — `RefreshCoordinator<T>` with `RefreshTarget<T>`: coalesces event-driven redraw requests.
- `types.ts` (101) + `index.ts` — `AgentSessionBrowserItem/Data/Options`, `AgentSetting`, `AgentModelOption`, `AgentWorkspaceBrowserItem`; the barrel re-exports `diagnosticText` from `tools/agent/presentation/text.ts`. Per the memory, **transcript projections live in `src/tools/agent/presentation/`, not here** — this package is view-only.

**`status/` (474 lines) — above-editor status.** Registered first in `src/index.ts` via `registerStatusWidget`.

- `widget.ts` (190) — `PiCoderStatusWidget` + `registerStatusWidget` + `STATUS_WIDGET_ID = "pi-coder-status"`. **One registration, two sections**: composes `AgentActivityWidget` and a lazily created `TodoListWidget`, keeps per-`EventBus` state in a `WeakMap`, and listens for typed snapshots on `pi-coder:status-agent` and `pi-coder:status-todo`. Domain modules only *publish*; this package alone owns widget registration and listeners.
- `agent-activity-widget.ts` (117) — `AgentActivityWidget`: two lines per run — spinner frame + run label + `mm:ss` elapsed + phase, then ` · `-joined tool counts, last action, and TODO progress; distinct rendering per `AgentRunStatus`, bounded by `MAX_PREVIEW_CHARS = 72` / `MAX_ACTIVITY_CHARS = 100`.
- `todolist-widget.ts` (31) — `TodoListWidget` rendering the full list.
- `format.ts` (54) / `agent-activity-format.ts` (31) — `formatTodoProgress`, `formatTodoList`, `oneLinePreview`, `firstLinePreview`, `formatToolCounts`.

---

### Tests

`test/{ask-user,inline-editor,multi-select,pager,select,select-with-message,dialog-queue}.test.ts` and `test/tui/{agent-session-browser,agent-workspace-browser,confirmation,overlay-stack,spinner}.test.ts`, with rendering pinned by file snapshots in `test/__snapshots__/` (`ask-user.*`, `select.*`, `pager.*`, `multi-select.*`, `select-with-message.content-page-{up,down}*.txt`, …) via `snapshotText`/`toMatchFileSnapshot`. The harness is `test/helpers.ts`: `mockTheme` identity theme, `KEY` raw key map, `press`/`type`/`paste`, `renderText()` (strips `CURSOR_MARKER`, renders inverse cursor as `[X]`), and **`interact()`, which re-renders after every keypress like the real TUI loop** — mandatory, because `InlineEditor`'s up/down reads render-computed visual-line state.
